h1: The 8 Best Printers for Small Spaces of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: the 8 best printers for small spaces, from shelf-friendly Canon inkjets to a compact laser and a portable thermal model.
summary: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 is the best all-round printer for tight spaces, with quiet inkjet printing and shelf-friendly placement. The TS6520 adds a small display and automatic duplex, the Brother HL-L2405W is the smallest footprint for documents only, and the MT610Pro thermal printer wins when storage space is the main problem.
intro: A printer for a small space is a different purchase than a printer for a house. The spec that decides it is where the thing will physically sit, and how loud it is when it wakes up two feet from your bed.
We ranked eight printers on the listing details: footprint claims, noise, connectivity and whether each can live on a shelf, in a corner or in a drawer. Pick by placement first, features second.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS4320 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact, quiet inkjet that fits a shelf or closet ledge.
products.description:
The TS4320 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one that prints, copies and scans over standard home wifi. The listing describes it as friendly to shelf, desk or closet-ledge placement, with a quieter inkjet mechanism.

It ranks first because it combines quiet operation with flexible placement at the $50-100 level. The TS6520 below adds a display and duplex, but those extras do not change how well it fits a small space.

Best for studio apartment living. Caveat: it is a basic model, so heavy printing is not what it is built for.
products.idealFor: Studio apartment dwellers who need quiet and flexible placement.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS6520 Wireless Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A small OLED screen and auto duplex for printers that sit across the room.
products.description:
The TS6520 is a compact inkjet whose standout is a tiny 1.42 inch OLED screen, plus automatic two-sided printing. It also keeps the quiet inkjet mechanism. Wireless is the standard module.

It trails the TS4320 only because it is built for features more than footprint. The display lets you check status from across the room.

Great for a printer that sits out of reach. Caveat: the listing does not claim a smaller body than the TS4320.
products.idealFor: Printers placed across the room from your desk.
products.skipIf: You do not need duplex printing.

products.name: Brother HL-L2405W Wireless Compact Monochrome Laser Printer
products.verdict: A smaller footprint than any compact inkjet here, for documents only.
products.description:
This is a print-only monochrome laser with a smaller footprint than the compact inkjet all-in-ones. It is Alexa compatible, and the toner does not dry out.

It ranks third because it prints but does not copy or scan, and it is louder during active printing. The no-dry-out toner is the real advantage over inkjets that sit unused.

Buy it for occasional document printing in a corner away from sleeping areas. Caveat: it does not print in color.
products.idealFor: Occasional document printers with a spare corner.
products.skipIf: You want to scan or print color.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact HP all-in-one with a three-month Instant Ink trial.
products.description:
The DeskJet 4355 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one with a standard wifi module, HP Smart app setup and a three-month HP Instant Ink trial. It prints, scans and copies.

It ranks behind the Canons because the listing makes no quiet-operation claim. Its setup via the HP Smart app is the easy part.

A fit for apartments where the printer sits far from the router. Caveat: the Instant Ink trial is only a trial, so plan for ink costs after it.
products.idealFor: Easy app-based setup in a small apartment.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: Auto feeder and fax in a compact body that works on the floor.
products.description:
The TR4720 includes an auto document feeder and built-in fax in a compact all-in-one body, with wireless via the Canon PRINT app. The listing says it works for floor or corner placement.

It ranks fifth because the feeder and fax add bulk that most small-space buyers will not use. They are useful for home-office paperwork.

Best where floor or corner placement is the only option. Caveat: expect a slightly larger body than the TS models.
products.idealFor: Small home offices with paperwork and little shelf space.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TS3720 Wireless All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: The smallest full all-in-one here, with no duplex.
products.description:
The TS3720 is a basic compact color all-in-one with the smallest footprint among the full all-in-one picks, a quiet inkjet mechanism and wireless via the Canon PRINT app. It has no auto duplex.

It sits below the TS4320 because the TS4320 lists more flexible placement. Here the trade is less hardware for a smaller body.

Pick it for noise-sensitive spaces on a tight budget. Caveat: you flip pages by hand for two-sided printing.

products.name: Canon Pixma MG3620 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: A compact inkjet with solid photo output and mobile printing.
products.description:
The MG3620 is a compact color inkjet all-in-one with mobile and tablet printing, a quiet inkjet mechanism, a standard wifi module and solid photo print quality per the listing. It sits in the $100-200 bracket.

It ranks lower because it costs more than the TS models without adding a space-saving advantage. Its photo strength is the reason to look at it.

Good for residents who print photos now and then. Caveat: it is the older design in this list.

products.name: Inkless Portable Bluetooth Thermal Printer (MT610Pro)
products.verdict: Stores in a drawer, but needs its own thermal paper.
products.description:
The MT610Pro is an inkless thermal printer at 300 DPI that supports Letter and A4 paper. It connects over Bluetooth, which sidesteps router range, and it stores in a drawer between uses.

It ranks last because it prints only on proprietary thermal paper and is a print-only device. It beats every other pick on storage.

Buy it for the tightest studios. Caveat: you are tied to thermal paper.
products.skipIf: You print daily and want standard paper.

whatMatters.detail: Shelf, desk, corner and drawer are different jobs. A shelf printer needs a small body, while a drawer printer needs to be portable. Check the listing's placement language before choosing.
Inkjets are quieter than lasers when printing. This matters in a studio where the printer sits near your bed or call area. Look for the words quiet mechanism in the bullets.
A standard wifi module needs router range, while Bluetooth does not. Check this if the printer will sit far from your router.
A document feeder and fax add bulk. If you never scan stacks of paper, skip them. Read the title for feeder or fax mentions.
Inkjets can dry out, toner does not, and thermal needs special paper. Pick the type that fits how often you print.

howToChoose.intro: Where the printer lives decides the model.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Quieter and does color. The Canon TS models, MG3620 and HP DeskJet 4355.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Smaller than compact inkjets and the toner does not dry out. The Brother HL-L2405W.

howToChoose.note: Most small-space buyers should default to an inkjet unless they print only black documents.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A quiet mechanism and a shelf-friendly body.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Canon PIXMA TS4320 lists both and is the pick here.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want duplex and a display, which the TS6520 adds, or photo quality from the MG3620.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: Light use. The TS3720 covers basics with the smallest all-in-one body.

faq.a: The Canon PIXMA TS models and the MG3620 list a quiet inkjet mechanism. The Brother laser is louder when printing.

faq.q: What mistake do small-space buyers make?
faq.a: Buying a feature-heavy model, then losing shelf space to a feeder they never use.

faq.q: Is a laser worth it over an inkjet?
faq.a: A laser's toner does not dry out and its footprint is smaller, but it prints black only here.

faq.q: How do I set up the Canon models?
faq.a: Use the Canon PRINT app over wifi. The HP DeskJet 4355 uses the HP Smart app.

faq.q: Does the thermal printer need ink?
faq.a: No, but it requires proprietary thermal paper.

faq.q: Can I keep the printer far from my router?
faq.a: Standard wifi models need range. The MT610Pro uses Bluetooth, which avoids that.

finalTake: For most small rooms, buy the Canon PIXMA TS4320. Step up to the TS6520 if you want duplex, or choose the Brother laser for document-only use. Only the MT610Pro solves a true storage problem, at the cost of special paper.
